basis: Printed SchmidtKaulp261name is nũũ, not DB nto. This directly matches nā́man after medial m nasalization/final-syllable loss; it is unmarked for stress. Primary reading restores cognacy independently of accent.

Printed SchmidtKaulp263smoke is duu (central/rounded vowel), not DB dre. It plausibly continues dhūmá with final m loss and deaspiration; compare local nasalization history. The source has no accent mark.

Printed SchmidtKaulp272mulberry ma'rõõṣ matches Shina marooc̣ and the full Turner9796 madhuravr̥kṣa sweet-fruit-tree family (Kho mrac̣h, Pal maharoc̣). Final stress occurs on the contracted tree component; exact transmission and nasalization remain open.

Printed Brokskat kunjaa nineteen appears alongside kunii in all Shina columns; full Turner2499ēkōnaviṁśati lists Gilgit kunīh and Pales ukənīh. The k selects the one-less compound branch independently of stress. Brokskat initial stress contrasts with Shina final kuníi; the final jaa extension remains a morphological/analogical residual.

Printed Brokskat lip is 'yṭi, not DB lyti: the supposed initial l was the stress mark. Rounded/front y plus retroflex ṭ and final i plausibly match oṣṭha/ooṭi lip after cluster simplification and fronting. Initial stress is secure, exact vowel-history relation provisional.

Ushojo g(h)iri stone matches girí rock/mountain. Full Turner4161explicitly gives Shina giri rock, so stone is not an ad hoc semantic extension. Optional aspiration and absence of stress marking are retained; inherited versus contact transmission is open.

Ushojo kimi insect directly matches kṛ́mi/krími, with r loss independently attested in Pali/Prakrit kimi in full Turner3438. Initial stress is a plausible inherited syllable correspondence, but regional borrowing cannot be excluded. This is stronger than an m-less kīṭa etymology.

Ushojo aso we (both inclusive and exclusive labels) matches the asmad oblique-derived paradigm. Full Turner986explicitly lists Guresi asõ and Shina asei alongside Palula asi. The modern first-syllable stress cannot be compared to a unique old headword accent because the old cases differ.

Ushojo likhona write contains likh plus modern on/a morphology. Full Turner11048distinguishes inherited likhati and passive/infinitival likhyate derivatives, including Punjabi/Hindi likhna. Contact versus inheritance and immediate formation are open, so no direct old-finite accent claim is made.

Printed Brokskat harvest is lɜɜs, not DB 'ɨɨs: initial l was misread as stress. Comparison with lunāti/lū harvest root is plausible and supported by Shina loon in the same table plus Palula lun in full Turner11082. Loss of n and recurring s citation morphology need a paradigm; no stress is printed.
